clue.text: High-flier up for trial?

parts.note: a high-flier is someone who flies aircraft, and being up for trial here means taking new aircraft up into the air to try them out, not facing a court

explanation.surface: An ambitious high achiever faces prosecution in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests a star performer and 'up for trial' suggests the dock; read literally, it is a flier who goes up to put new aircraft through their paces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: an aviator whose job is flying untried aircraft to assess their performance.

clue.text: Coach tour arranged, crossing heart of Montana

indicators.note: crossing means the rearranged letters straddle the other piece, holding it inside
arranged means the letters of the word tour are put into a new order
heart of picks the central letter of the seven-letter word Montana

explanation.surface: A coach trip is organised that passes through the middle of the US state of Montana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach tour' reads as a bus holiday, but 'Coach' is the definition. 'arranged' turns TOUR into TUOR, which is crossing the T at the heart of Montana.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to coach someone is to teach or train them privately, which is what a private teacher does.

clue.text: Piece of sports equipment found in dumpster, incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a dumpster is a large rubbish container, called a skip in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone finds a bit of sports kit thrown out in a rubbish container.
explanation.walkthrough: A SKIP is the British name for a builder's open rubbish container; 'incomplete' drops its last letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of a pair of long runners worn on the feet for gliding over snow is sporting equipment.

clue.text: Having a litre in bar is common

indicators.note: in means the article and the litre abbreviation are placed inside the word for bar

parts.note: to bar something is to prevent it

explanation.surface: Ordering a litre of drink at the pub is a usual thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means to stop or prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something widespread or generally occurring is described as common.

clue.text: Endure the French drink

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
stout is a dark beer, a drink

explanation.surface: Put up with a French beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to survive or keep going until the very end of something is to endure it.

clue.text: Violent storm encountered on the way up –- bother!

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the way up means the word for encountered is read from bottom to top

parts.note: encountered means met
a pest is a bother or nuisance

explanation.surface: Someone is caught in a fierce storm while climbing and mutters an oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns MET into TEM; 'bother!' looks like an exclamation but is a noun for a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a severe gale with heavy rain or wind is a storm of great force.

clue.text: Self-satisfied son, sucker

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
a mug is a gullible person, a sucker

explanation.surface: A smug son turns out to be a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: complacent and pleased with oneself means self-satisfied.

clue.text: Welsh channel broadcast a minister holding a first in theology

indicators.note: holding means the shuffled letters keep the theology initial inside them
broadcast means scattered, so the collected letters are rearranged
first in picks the opening letter of the word theology

explanation.surface: A cleric with a top theology degree goes on air on a Welsh TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges A MINISTER and A into MENAISRAIT, which is holding T (the first in theology). 'channel' suggests television but is a sea strait.
explanation.definitionFit: The Menai Strait is the narrow sea passage separating Anglesey from mainland Wales.

clue.text: Info attached to cane carrying mature plant

indicators.note: attached to joins the two pieces side by side
carrying means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
mature means old
a cane is a rod

explanation.surface: Gardening advice about tying a fully grown plant to a supporting stick.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN (British slang for information) carrying OLD makes GOLDEN, which is attached to ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tall garden perennial with yellow flower sprays is a plant.

clue.text: To kill a king

parts.note: to off someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: A plot to assassinate a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a ruler of the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia was a monarch.

clue.text: Dull ending of secret ceremony

indicators.note: ending of picks the final letter of the word secret

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: The conclusion of a hidden ritual turns out to be boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hackneyed and unoriginal remarks are dull from overuse.

clue.text: Supposing that, entering important round of cup

indicators.note: entering means this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: seminal means highly important and influential
if means supposing that

explanation.surface: A conditional remark that a key cup match is coming up.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the penultimate stage of a knockout competition is one round of a cup.

clue.text: Long and complicated procedure investing millions in capital function

indicators.note: investing here means clothing or surrounding, so the capital wraps round the next piece

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
a role is a function

explanation.surface: A financial process of putting millions into a city's capital fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' and 'capital' suggest finance, but the capital is a city, RIGA, which 'investing' clothes around M.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tedious, convoluted rigmarole is an overlong procedure full of needless steps.

clue.text: Urchin, for example, raised to pocket absolute bargain

indicators.note: to pocket means to take inside, so the reversed abbreviation surrounds the rest
raised in a down clue means the abbreviation is read upwards

parts.note: utter means absolute or complete
a snip is British slang for a bargain

explanation.surface: A street child, say, is brought up to steal an outright bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EG into GE, which pockets UTTER plus SNIP (British for a bargain).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ragged, poorly brought-up child of the streets is an urchin.

clue.text: A wing that's out of the way

parts.note: a side of a building or team is a wing

explanation.surface: A building's wing that stands somewhere remote.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something set apart or to one side is placed out of the way.

clue.text: One in clear case

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the word for clear

parts.note: patent means clear or obvious
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single example of an open-and-shut matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear case' reads as a phrase, but 'clear' is wordplay and 'case' is the definition, a medical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a doctor's case is a person under medical care.

clue.text: Father caught in lot with RR, a suspect vehicle

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: in means the cricket abbreviation goes inside the word lot
suspect means dubious or unsound, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A father is caught on a car lot with a Rolls-Royce, a dodgy motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges LOT, RR and A into TROLAR, and C goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a police car on its beat is one kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Tout upset priest after Towcester's first

indicators.note: after means the rearranged priest comes after the opening letter
first picks the opening letter of the word Towcester's
upset means the letters of priest are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A racing tout irritates a clergyman at Towcester racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Towcester is an English town with a racecourse. 'upset' rearranges PRIEST into IPSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a racing tout sells betting predictions, the trade of someone who gives tips.

clue.text: London theatre element

definitions.meaning: a famous variety venue in London's West End
a silvery metal of the platinum group, number 46

explanation.surface: A London playhouse and a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: both the West End theatre and the chemical metal bear this name.

clue.text: Awful threat involving English playhouse

indicators.note: involving means containing the next piece
awful means dreadful, so the letters of threat are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreadful menace in an English playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges THREAT into THEATR, which is involving E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a building where plays are staged is a playhouse.

clue.text: Bit of breakfast with chief boffin

parts.note: an egg is a typical item at breakfast
a head is a chief

explanation.surface: The boss scientist at the breakfast table.
explanation.walkthrough: A boffin is British slang for a scientist or expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an intellectual, bookish expert is informally called a boffin.

clue.text: Duck taken from shopping precinct -– charge wife denied

parts.note: a mall is a shopping precinct

indicators.note: denied means the abbreviation for wife is refused, so taken away

parts.note: a ward is someone in one's charge

explanation.surface: A duck is removed from a shopping centre and a wife is refused a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests a fee, but it is a WARD in someone's care; 'denied' removes W.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the common wild duck with a green-headed drake is a kind of duck.

clue.text: French dramatist's further entertaining story

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: more means further, additional
a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A French playwright's next amusing tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like an adjective for a story but means holding.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the seventeenth-century comic playwright of Tartuffe was a French dramatist.

clue.text: Start working with group

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Starting to work with a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the beginning of something, especially something unpleasant, is its start.

clue.text: Quality of sound from saxophonist on euphonium?

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A saxophone player tries out a euphonium and is judged on the sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across saxophonisT ON Euphonium.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the timbre of a musical note is its sound quality.

clue.text: Bravery of everyone locked in tower

indicators.note: locked in means shut inside the next piece

parts.note: a gantry is a tower-like framework, as for launching rockets
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The courage of people all trapped inside a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: courageous behaviour, especially in battle, is bravery.

clue.text: Return from investment unknown, criminal lied

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: criminal means bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An investor's returns are uncertain because a crook told lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges LIED into IELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the income an investment produces is its return.

clue.text: Customers tell niece off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shoppers rebuke a girl's aunt's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tell off' reads as scold, but 'off' rearranges TELL NIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the body of a business's clients are its customers.

clue.text: Publish thin paper once time runs out

indicators.note: runs out means the time abbreviation departs from the word

parts.note: tissue is thin paper

explanation.surface: Print on flimsy paper once the deadline passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bring out a book or statement officially is to publish it.

clue.text: Quarrel briefly in hydro

indicators.note: briefly means shortened, losing the last letter

parts.note: a spat is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A short row breaks out at a health resort.
explanation.walkthrough: A hydro is a British term for a hotel offering water treatments.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a resort with mineral springs or health treatments is a hydro.

clue.text: Part of film is true, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: real means true or genuine

explanation.surface: A section of a movie is said to be authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a spool holding a length of cinema film is one part of the film.

clue.text: Sleep in Happy Valley?

definitions.meaning: the imaginary world one enters in slumber
an idyllic place of fantasy, a land of reverie, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Nodding off in a pleasant valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the state of sleep and an ideal fantasy place both get this name.
